Explain me zener diode in simple terms and give a tabular difference between avalance breakown
 and zener breakdown

A **Zener diode** is a special type of diode that allows current to flow not only in the forward direction (like a normal diode) but also in the reverse direction when the voltage exceeds a certain value called the **Zener breakdown voltage**. This feature makes it useful in voltage regulation. When the reverse voltage reaches a certain value (the Zener voltage), the diode maintains a stable voltage across it, even if the current changes.

### Difference between Avalanche Breakdown and Zener Breakdown

| Aspect                   | Zener Breakdown                               | Avalanche Breakdown                           |
|--------------------------|-----------------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------|
| **Mechanism**             | Direct rupture of covalent bonds due to a strong electric field. | Caused by the collision of accelerated carriers (electrons/holes) with atoms, generating more charge carriers. |
| **Doping**                | Heavily doped                                  | Lightly doped                                  |
| **Breakdown Voltage**     | Occurs at lower voltages, typically less than 6V | Occurs at higher voltages, generally above 6V |
| **Depletion Region Width**| Narrow depletion region                       | Wide depletion region                         |
| **Temperature Coefficient** | Negative (breakdown voltage decreases with increasing temperature) | Positive (breakdown voltage increases with increasing temperature) |
| **Usage**                 | Primarily used in Zener diodes for voltage regulation | Rarely used for specific high-voltage applications |
| **Current**               | Sharp increase in current                     | Gradual increase in current                    |

Zener breakdown dominates at low voltages (less than 6V) and avalanche breakdown occurs at higher voltages【5†source】.
